name: @kobai/core
description: The kobai packages a Project depends on.
// publishConfig: This package is published, because a generated Project depends on it as an ordinary versioned dependency and `workspace:*` does not resolve outside this workspace (ADR-0034). `private: true` used to be the only thing standing between a stray `pnpm publish` and npmjs.com, so removing it puts something else there: `registry` pins publishing at a loopback address, which is where `devbox run ci` stands one up. A publish to the public registry therefore has to be a deliberate act — someone passing `--registry` on purpose — rather than a typo. tests/publish-guard.test.ts fails the build if this pin goes missing.
// bin: `kobai-upgrade` is the command ADR-0001 has always described — a version bump plus the shipped codemods. It is a bin of *this* package rather than of `create-kobai` because the codemods that run must be the ones the version being upgraded **to** ships, and this is the only package that is at that version in a Project once the install has run. See docs/adr/0035-upgrading-is-a-command-kobai-ships.md.
// exports: `./codemods` is what a Project's `node_modules` is asked for during an upgrade, so it is the set belonging to the version arrived at rather than the one the running command came from. `./package.json` is what tells the upgrade command which version that is; Node only lets a package be asked for its own manifest when `exports` names it.

scripts.// openapi:generate: It needs no build and no database. Node runs the TypeScript directly (type stripping), `createKobai` builds its pool without connecting, and the description is a property of the routes rather than of anything behind them. `devbox run openapi:generate` runs this and then regenerates @kobai/client from what it wrote — in that order, because pnpm walks the workspace in dependency order.
scripts.// db:migrate: There is no db:migrate script either, for a smaller reason. Core applies its own migrations at boot, so the CLI would be a second code path applying the same files — and ADR-0030 records that the CLI and the programmatic migrator default to different tracking schemas. `drizzle.config.ts` still sets the tracking location explicitly so the two agree if one is ever added.
scripts.// db:push: There is deliberately no db:push script — not here, not in any Plugin, and not in the reference Project. `drizzle-kit push` diffs a schema against the LIVE database, so pushing Core's schema at a database holding Plugin tables reports `[/] Changes applied` and silently DROPS every Plugin table, while leaving their migration tracking rows intact so the migration runner believes the work is done and cannot repair it. Observed, not theorised: see FINDINGS.md section E on branch prototype/drizzle-multi-migration, and docs/adr/0030-generate-and-migrate-only-never-drizzle-kit-push.md. `tablesFilter` mitigates it and is set below anyway, but the primary control is that the dangerous command is never available.
